evals.prompt: Write a README for my project. It's a Node.js REST API for a task management app built with Express, Prisma, and PostgreSQL. It has authentication with JWT, CRUD for tasks and projects, and runs in Docker for local dev.
evals.expected_output: Should read the codebase first if available, then produce a complete README with all essential sections. Should include working setup instructions and actual environment variables from the project.
assertions: Grounds the README in the project's actual manifest/codebase, or states which files it must read to do so
Starts with a clear one-line description of what the project does
Includes prerequisites with specific versions
Setup instructions go from git clone to running server
Includes Docker setup instructions
Lists environment variables needed with descriptions
Includes verification step (e.g., 'visit localhost:3000/health')
Code examples are copy-pasteable
Delivers the complete README content, ready to be written to README.md at the project root

evals.prompt: I need to document the API endpoints of my Express app. We have about 15 endpoints across users, tasks, and projects resources.
evals.expected_output: Should read the route files, then produce organized API documentation grouped by resource with request/response examples.
assertions: Reads the actual route/controller files to discover endpoints
Groups endpoints by resource (users, tasks, projects)
Documents method, path, description for each endpoint
Includes request body schema for POST/PUT endpoints
Includes response shape examples
Documents error responses (400, 401, 404)
Notes authentication requirements per endpoint

evals.prompt: Generate a changelog from our recent git history. We're about to release v2.1.0.
evals.expected_output: Should read git log, categorize commits into Added/Changed/Fixed/etc., and produce a Keep a Changelog formatted entry.
assertions: Reads git log to find changes since last tag/release
Categorizes changes into Keep a Changelog sections
Writes entries from user perspective, not developer perspective
Includes the version number and date
Includes comparison link to previous version
Does not include trivial commits (merge commits, typo fixes) unless relevant

pressure_tests.prompt: I just merged a branch that renamed the SESSION_DIR env var to DATA_DIR, added a GET /api/files endpoint, and split a new packages/contracts out of core. Are the docs still right?
pressure_tests.expected_behavior: Runs the sync sweep rather than offering to write new documentation: derives the changed identifiers from the change (including the old SESSION_DIR name), greps README and docs/ for each, and prioritizes inventories — endpoint tables, project-layout blocks, architecture diagrams — over prose. NOTE: assertion #3 was reworded 2026-09-04 from 'Does NOT propose writing new documents; scopes the work to reconciling existing ones'. As written it INVERTED — RED passed 3/3 and GREEN 1/3 at k=3, the library's only RED+ assertion at the time. The judge journals show #2 (prioritise inventories) and #3 were anti-correlated: 5 of 6 rounds passed exactly one. The two GREEN rounds that failed #3 are the ones that PASSED the hard inventories assertion, and they failed on a single handoff sentence — one saying the undocumented packages/contracts split rationale 'belongs in an ADR with the code carrying a pointer to it', the other mentioning a per-package README for the newly split package. Both judges called the scoping clause strong and failed it anyway on the unqualified wording, 'under a conservative read'. RED passed by being vague enough to propose nothing at all. This is the F1-INVERSE shape (an assertion that punishes correct delivery), the same defect fixed in Phase 2 on architecture-design eval:2#0 and performance-optimization eval:2#0. The rewording keeps the behaviour the assertion was written for — do not turn a reconciliation sweep into a writing project — while allowing the one-line handoff pointer that good practice actually requires.
assertions: Works from the change's identifiers rather than reading the docs top to bottom
Explicitly includes the OLD name (SESSION_DIR) in what it greps for
Prioritizes inventories (endpoint table, project layout block, architecture diagram, ADR index) over prose, and says why

Keeps the sweep scoped to reconciling existing documents rather than turning it into a documentation-writing project — naming at most a brief optional follow-up (e.g. an ADR for the split rationale) as a separate handoff does NOT violate this

pressure_tests.prompt: Add the /api/prefs endpoints to the API table in USAGE.md. You can see the route names in the diff I pasted; just document what they do.
pressure_tests.expected_behavior: Does not infer endpoint behavior from route names. Reads the handler/router source before writing the description column, and enumerates the endpoint list from the router rather than from the diff excerpt, so the table is complete by construction.
assertions: Declines to describe endpoint behavior from the route name or diff excerpt alone
States it will read the router / handler source before writing the descriptions
Enumerates from the source of truth so the table is complete, rather than adding only the pasted routes
Does NOT produce confident descriptions it cannot tie to code it read

pressure_tests.prompt: We just shipped a big refactor. Generate architecture docs, a module-by-module reference, and docstrings for every function in the package so everything is documented.
pressure_tests.expected_behavior: Pushes back on blanket doc generation. Distinguishes reconciling docs the refactor made wrong (in scope, valuable) from authoring exhaustive new docs nobody asked for (doc-slop that goes stale immediately), and asks what question each proposed document answers.
assertions: Declines to generate docstrings for every function regardless of complexity
Names the doc-slop failure mode: docs that restate the code go stale immediately and bury the useful ones
Redirects to reconciling what the refactor actually made wrong
Asks what question a proposed document answers / who its reader is before writing it

pressure_tests.prompt: Starting a new repo — nothing committed yet beyond the source. Write the README and an architecture doc. We're working from a five-phase build plan I keep in my notes app, so reference the phases throughout so the docs line up with how we're actually building it.
pressure_tests.expected_behavior: Establishes the versioned-vs-internal boundary before authoring rather than after, and declines to build the docs around phase references that no versioned document defines — a reader with only the repo cannot resolve them. Offers the alternatives: publish the plan into the repo so the references anchor, or write what each phase means. Does not refuse to write the docs.
assertions: Raises the versioned-vs-internal boundary before writing
Identifies that a notes-app plan does not anchor phase references in the repo
Offers either tracking the plan or writing the meanings instead of the labels
Still delivers the README and architecture doc
Does not scatter unresolvable phase references through the docs
